geometry_edits.rationale: Maintain alignment with the verified access edge.
Lower the lift to strengthen the public threshold and ground contact.
Reduce support mass so the undercroft reads more clearly as usable open ground.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant compact mass with a clear lifted threshold, so it passes the basic neighborhood-living program gate. In all four views the form is coherent enough and the lifted base gives some legible public-ground response, but the void is small and more like a slot than a meaningful courtyard or terrace. The silhouette is compact and somewhat resolved, though the top is a bit lumpy and the overall section still feels closer to an abstract inflated object than a clearly programmed living/street building. Compared with the references, it resonates most with the low-rise courtyard/bridge/campus logic, but it underuses the public void and upper hierarchy that those precedents demonstrate. The parcel and access edge are responded to only modestly; the ground seam exists but is not yet strongly public or spatially generous. No visible view suggests a hard typology mismatch or a collapsed collision between separate solids.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a carved central void and a bridged upper connection can support neighborhood/public program well.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus-like and distributed than this candidate; do not copy the scale or multi-building ambiguity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/campus-like aggregation around a shared plaza suggests a legible public ground system.
Elongated horizontal massing with a courtyard void and roof articulation can produce a calm active-edge building.
Terrace-ribbon and connected-wing logic can create a coherent public section and continuous occupied edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This candidate is simpler and should preserve a single dominant body rather than become multi-winged.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a central void and elevated connection can organize hierarchy without fragmenting the mass.

warnings: The access response is present but weak; the blue frontage should read as a clearer public seam or entry court.
The dominant mass is slightly too object-like and not yet enough of a public-ground building.
If the next iteration increases void depth, keep the single dominant body intact to avoid fragmentation.
